# 2 Baruch Chapter 78 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** Baruch's Letters
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 78:1 — epistolary greeting formula

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "Thus-speaks Baruch the-son-of-Neriah... Mercy-and-peace be-to-you" |
| LOGOS | "Thus speaks Baruch the son of Neriah... mercy and peace be to you" |
| PNEUMA | "Baruch son of Neriah speaks... May mercy and peace be yours" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** SOPHIA adopted LOGOS. The Syriac opening formula hkana amar ('Thus speaks') is a standard epistolary convention preserved by LOGOS; PNEUMA's rearrangement loses the formal address structure.

---

## 78:3 — dissolution of the world

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "all-we-who-are-in-the-world... will-be-dissolved" |
| LOGOS | "all of us who are in the world that now is will be dissolved" |
| PNEUMA | "all of us who exist in this present world will pass away" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** SOPHIA adopted LOGOS. 'Dissolved' (Syriac: netpsakun) is a specific cosmological term for the dissolution of the present order; PNEUMA's 'pass away' is too soft for the radical eschatological language.

---

## 78:5 — transience metaphors

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "will-pass-away as-a-cloud, and-as-a-vapor will-it-vanish-away" |
| LOGOS | "will pass away as a cloud, and as a vapor will it vanish away" |
| PNEUMA | "will vanish like a cloud, and disappear like a vapor" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** SOPHIA adopted LOGOS. The Syriac uses two different verbs (pass away/vanish); LOGOS preserves both. PNEUMA uses the same verb twice ('vanish/disappear'), losing the original's variety.

---
